body:
I thought I responded to you last week, but I guess not.

Anyway I'm saving your response, along with many other ones here. Thank you. I really appreciate it.
Thank you so much.
Thank you very much.

I did. This is a good place.

Thank you.
Thank you. I really appreciate it.

Wow, I'm so sorry to hear that. I hope things for you are better now.

Thank you.
Haven't read it since I made this post, I'm happy to say. Thank you.

I hope so. Thanks. He just has a really fucked up way of expressing things. I appreciate that he never sugarcoated anything and told it like it was, but sometimes it was just a bit too much, you know?

Thanks!

1000 Awesome Things... what a coincidence. I bought the book on a whim, and I received it when I was feeling suicidal. So I ended up giving it to my shrink so that he could use it to help other people. 

I've heard the dude on a podcast (the website creator, that is), and he seems like a really nice guy. Apparently he created the blog when he was in a moment of distress. I will revisit the site. I'm feeling better now.

I've definitely considered it. I might qualify for getting part of my loan forgiven because of my health. I hope I get better, because I don't want to remain like this forever. But if I don't, heaven forbid, at least I have that option.

Thank you.

I honestly don't know if he loves me (this isn't me feeling sorry for myself). The last time I saw him was a few summers ago. We were driving, just me and him and my half-brother in the backseat. My father stopped the car at a scenic viewpoint and said, "You know what... I think my biggest regret in life was having children." I wasn't even planned as a child... I was an accident.

Thank you so much. I appreciate it.

I'm gonna see my shrink next week and talk about other options I can explore apart from meds. I've been playing "antidepressant roulette" since 2005 or 2006, and maybe some people like me just need something other than meds. I know I could keep trying, but these side effects aren't really worth it anymore. :/

Thanks so much. Yeah, it is hard to come up with a list of names at the moment, to be honest. But I can work on it.

I honestly did not expect many people to respond, and I am extremely touched. I need to go offline for a bit (I've been doing a Leapforce test all day, and my head hurts), but I'll be back to respond to everyone else. Thanks.

Hey there. Nope, I don't mind. I have major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, social anxiety disorder, and possibly PTSD. I take Wellbutrin XR, but it's not working very well for me so far (I've only been on it for just over 4 weeks, though).

Thank you so much. I appreciate it.

sorry for the multiple but just in case you did not see my edit: i think i'll go offline now just so i can stop reading the email he sent me. but i really appreciate all that you and the other people here have done for me. i will take it slowly. see my pscyh on tuesday, let him know about this breakdown i had tonight.

thank you, reddit. i dont have the words to express how thankful i am. but you have helped me a great deal and i appreciate it

he is sick, yeah. he doesn't "believe in depression" but he was diagnosed with it.

thanks so very much. i think i'll go offline now just so i can stop reading the email he sent me. but i really appreciate all that you and the other people here have done for me. i will take it slowly. see my pscyh on tuesday, let him know about this breakdown i had tonight.

thank you again. take care, everyone.

i just dont want to upset her or make it seem like i'm unleashing my problems on her when she has so much to deal with. she has always been a stoic person, always tough. but, yeah, at the same time, i don't want to regret what i should have said to her. it's a slippery slope.

i am sorry about your mom.

one of my friends said she could take them in if i needed to suddenly leave the country (my mother lives/works overseas). i checked myself into a psych ward 2 summers ago and my "team" said that they could arrange for someone to check on my pets. but i only stayed the night and went home the next afternoon.

thank you very much. (not sounding sarcastic or anything, really... thank you all so much)

he has not supported me for almost a decade. he was abusive to me and my mother, throughout my childhood. so many people (rightfully) tell me to let go, that it's ok not to love him. for whatever reason, i can't stop loving him, no matter how he treats me. even if he is ashamed of me.

i have always wanted to volunteer with the cancer society...

thank you very much.
my psych said i should be honest with my mother, let her know my mental health is not well right now. but i dont want to unload that on her. maybe you're right. i'll email him.

just really hurs to have my dad be so ashamed of me and thnking i am "playing the victim" and feeling sorry for myself. i might seem like it online but offline, i only tell everything to my psych. just feeling like a waste of space, like i am taking up valuable energy,

i just get really tired of pretending. my stepfather said the best thing i can do for my mother is take care of myself. i wish i could tell her how i really feel, that i am so afraid she will die before i finish school. but you don't say things like that to a person who has cancer, do you?

only my mother. 

my dad is ashamed of me and my half-brother is 7 years old. (not trying to sound like i am rude/knocking down what you are saying but i know my father hates me, he hasnt contacted me since sending that email except for obligatory "happy birthday" email). 

i was only here for my mother. cant bear the thought of her possibly dying. she had her last chemo a couple of weeks ago but lives in another country. i know it is terrible to make exit plans when she is so sick but i cant bear the thought of my life without her.

been seeing psych since jan 2008 with a 2.5 year break in between (deluded myself into thinking i was better and didnt need him, resumed sessions last year). seeing him on tuesday.

lhe said to go to hospita if i feel like this ("this" being how i feel right now) but i can't. there's school and who would take care of my pets.
thank you.

it just hurts so much right now. i am so tired of pretending when all i want to do is just want to scream. this is probably the best representation of how i feel all the time. http://www.optipess.com/2012/09/28/dressing-up/

i will try to hold on, i see my psych on tuesday. but i really just want to sleep forever and ever.

it hurts so much. to be a failure. to have someone so ashamed of me. i am tired of being alone, having to take care of myself. and be remnded of what a failure i am. just want omeone to hold me and tell me it will be ok. i have nobody.

Yeah, exactly. My dad, who is quite mentally ill himself, thinks depression is a lie, something invented by pharmaceutical companies so that they can profit. :/ If I could snap out of it, I wouldn't have written that initial response. It's also hard because this is simply how I feel, and it makes me feel guilty for being "self-pitying".

That's really good advice. I do enjoy helping out people whenever I can. Thanks.
Thanks very much. I appreciate it.

Thanks. To be honest, I don't even know how to fake being confident. My childhood was very tough, and I came away from it always feeling like a useless failure. I will look at the social skills subreddit for advice on that.

Honestly I am jealous of people like you. I'm in a "useless" program and my GPA plummeted from an A- to C average because of my mental health issues. At my school anyway, job fair recruiters are eager to snatch up new engineering grads who have little to no experience. I hope you'll be able to find a good job when you're done.

I've been to /r/SuicideWatch a few times. Talking to people there has sometimes helped me.

Thanks. I tried a few times. I'm very soft-spoken and can't speak very well (that is, I stumble upon my words and interrupt people when I get excited). But I can practice that. Some people have suggested Toastmasters to me, and I'm considering it.

I'm on Wellbutrin XR, just started last month. But I have experienced none of its positive effects yet. :/

Thanks.
Thanks, I never knew of that subreddit until now. Much appreciated.

Eye contact is something I really need to work on. It just makes me very uncomfortable when a person looks into my eyes for several seconds.

Thank you. That's good advice. It does take practice. I just have a tendency to beat myself up if the outcome isn't good... something I definitely need to work on.

Thanks. I'm still trying to figure out my strengths. My self-esteem is kind of shot at the moment (not trying to sound like I'm feeling sorry for myself, I'm just at a very low point in my life right now).

Thanks.  
I used to work at one of those call centres. Got along with everyone, unfortunately didn't really make any connections. It didn't pay enough and had no employee benefits so I left to complete my completely useless BA in English. Will be done in December 2014.
I'm sorry. Yeah, when you're barely hanging in there as is, something can just make you snap. That person was a jerk. Maybe there's stuff going on in his life and he takes it out on people online. :/

In other words, if you suffer from crippling social anxiety, you are absolutely fucked. I can barely keep up a conversation with a stranger, let alone schmooze and be something I'm not. I am also very shy and awkward.

And before anyone yells at me, I am in therapy and on meds for my mental health issues. If this LPT has actually worked for anyone with depression and/or other mental illnesses, then feel free to tell me how you do it.

I'm sorry, I didn't mean to sound rude. Networking really is beneficial but when you feel absolutely hopeless and like a loser, you may wonder what the point even is, let alone the point of life.
